text:
jihoon: Bringing up open-model-x v2 on int8/PTQ, noticed weird token splits around fullwidth brackets and leading/trailing spaces in CJK. Repro and a short eval below.

maya: can you paste a minimal repro? quick check: tokenizer config, merge ops, anything changed in vocab?

jihoon: minimal repro: `tokenizer.encode('（你好）')` on f16 baseline -> `[10123, 4521, 9876, 102]` but on int8-ptq run -> `[10123, 45, 21, 9876, 102]` (extra split between bracket and char). Happens for `「」` and fullwidth comma `，` too.

tariq: that looks like a byte-alignment issue from quantized embedding lookup or a different pre-tokenization step. Is this only on the compiled runtime path or also in Python tokenizer?

jihoon: only observed in fully compiled inference path (runtime AOT kernels). Python tokenizer (hf tokenizers) is consistent. Suspect an off-by-one in the pre-tokenization trimming that runs in the runtime's unicode handling.

eva: what does eval look like? BLEU or chrF numbers?

jihoon: quick eval on small zh->en testset: float16 baseline chrF 58.3, int8 PTQ chrF 49.7. BLEU dropped 3.2 -> 1.6 on same seed. Most diffs are around punctuation/brackets and leading spaces in multi-sentence inputs. Example diff:  
```
src: 他对（这个）系统很满意。
baseline: He was satisfied with (this) system.
int8-ptq: He was satisfied with ( this ) system .
```
notice the added spaces inside parentheses and separated punctuation tokens.

maya: ok that's high impact. Could be tokenizer detok expectations vs runtime detokenizer. Do we run any detok in postprocessing on the runtime?

jihoon: runtime only returns token ids, we do detok in the client but the token ids themselves changed. So the model's outputs use space tokens where baseline did not.

tariq: can you dump the token id sequences around the punctuation for several examples? also run `--tokenize-debug` on the runtime to compare byte offsets.

jihoon: dumping now for 10 examples, attached in the log. quick sample: `[(101, \"（\"), (205, \" \"), (9876, \"你\"), ...]` vs baseline `[(101, \"（\"), (9876, \"你\"), ...]`. So an extra token id 205 (space) appears after the bracket.

eva: could this be an interaction with KV-cache alignment or kernel that merges subword offsets? Maybe the KV cache indices get shifted and we re-tokenize partial prefixes differently on streaming vs non-streaming. Any correlation with sequence length?

jihoon: seems more common at shorter prefixes when caching is warmed. Less frequent at long prefix lengths. Also more common on compiled binned kernels (small batch optimized path).

tariq: action plan: 1) run tokenizer unit tests on compiled runtime codepath (we have a docker image with tools) 2) bisect commit range for the compile-time unicode normalizer change 3) add targeted eval focusing on brackets, ZWJ, ZWNJ, and fullwidth punctuation. I'll take 1 and 2.

maya: I'll add an eval harness job and scoreboard row that computes token boundary delta and common edit examples. If we can reproduce deterministically we can link to a regression PR.

eva: small mitigation: add a runtime fallback that forces use of Python tokenization on any inputs containing these chars (\u3000-\u303F, ZWJ/ZWNJ) until we have a fix. Not ideal for perf but useful for canary customers.

jihoon: agreed. we should also check quantization config: qlinear vs symmetric, and embedding table shard offsets. PTQ step used per-tensor calibrations; I'm adding an experiment to try q4_j8 hybrid and see if mapping difference persists.

infra-bot: deploy job #3421 queued: `eng-ml/tokenizer-rt-debug` image -> staging. Notify in ~10m when logs available. :gear:

maya: thanks, please add me as reviewer on the bisect PR. I'll also push a small test into our eval-suite: sample pairs for `（`, `）`, `「`, `」`, `，`, `。`, and Arabic/Hebrew punctuation (to catch RTL spacing).

jihoon: note: found one odd case with RTL marker: Hebrew + Arabic mark plus punctuation caused token reorder on output: `...‏.` became `.‏ ...` in some runs. Not sure if detokenizer handles RTL markers correctly after kernel-level merges. adding to test matrix.

tariq: good catch. if detok is wrong in client layer due to different token id ordering we'll need a deterministic detok that is independent of locale assumptions.

eva: next steps: tarball logs + small failing examples -> put under /eng-ml/regressions/1998765432 for triage. assign owner jihoon for reproducer and tariq for bisect.

jihoon: will upload repro set and a short script `repro_token_split.sh` with `HF_TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false` and runtime flags.

maya: great. mark as P0 for bring-up until we confirm forward/backwards compatibility. :exclamation:

eva: if fallback reduces perf too much we can enable it only for affected customers via routing policy.

jihoon: thanks all, will post logs when infra-bot finishes.
